findings.reason: Confirmed (high). The arXiv v2 TeX of Lemma 5.17 (label local_ring_def_ring) reads 'if x ∈ \Xbar ∖ Y then \hat{\OO}_{X,x}\br{T} ≅ R^□_{G,ρ_x}'. The completed local ring is that of the total space X, not of X̄, and the published p. 35 agrees. Item /32 writes Ô_{X̄,x}⟦T⟧. That ring is killed by ϖ, whereas R^□_{G,ρ_x} is flat over the mixed-characteristic coefficient ring, so the item's isomorphism cannot hold. The fix is right, and Lemma 15.11(2) (p. 80) gives the separate special-fibre version.

Confirmed (high). On published p. 76 the paper says 'The map Z(G^0) → G/G′ is a central isogeny by [19, Corollary 5.3.3]' and 'the map Z_i → H_i is an isogeny'. The proof of Proposition 15.1 adds 'the natural map q: G → H is a central isogeny as Z_1 → H_1 is an isogeny'. Item /4 copies these claims. When Δ = G/G^0 ≠ 1, the groups G/G′ and H_i are disconnected, while the image of a connected torus lies in the identity component, so these maps are not surjective and are not isogenies. In the red team's example G = G_m × C_2, the map Z_1 = G_m → H_1 = G_m × C_2 misses a component. Conrad's Corollary 5.3.3 concerns connected reductive groups. The fix is right: use Z_i → H_i^0, and require only what Proposition 8.7 needs of q. I also checked the side remark on Proposition 13.25 (p. 68): 'Since Z(G^0) is a split torus' fails for G^0 = SL_2, whose centre is μ_2. Diagonalizability suffices for the decomposition used there.

Confirmed (high). On published p. 85 (arXiv v2 TeX lines 6415–6418) the paper writes Hom^cont((Γ_F^{ab,p} ⊗ M_2)^Δ, Q̄_p^×) ≅ H^1(Γ_F, H_2^0(Q̄_p)), with Γ_F three times, while (93) and the cited [PQ25] use Γ_E^{ab,p}. Item /77 copies the Γ_F form. The subscript matters. Δ acts on Γ_F^{ab} trivially, by inner conjugation, so for the sign lattice M and p odd the Γ_F-invariants vanish. The unrestricted isomorphism with all of H^1 is false as well: for M = Z and E = F, an unramified character of order 2 (p odd) lies in H^1(Γ_F, Q̄_p^×) but cannot factor through the pro-p group Γ_F^{ab,p}. The fix is right: use Γ_E, and restrict to deformations of the fixed residual, via principal-unit cocycles after the Teichmüller twist, rather than all of H^1.

Confirmed (high). Item /81 states that admissible Galois parameters Γ_F → ^LT, 'equivalently H^1(Γ_F, T̂(Q̄_p))', correspond to all continuous characters T(F) → Q̄_p^×. Birkbeck's p-adic correspondence (JTNB, https://jtnb.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.5802/jtnb.1114.pdf, the admissible homomorphisms on PDF p. 5) uses the Weil group W_{K/F}. The red team's counterexample is right. For T = G_m, the continuous character χ(x) = p^{v_F(x)} has unbounded image, while a continuous character of the compact group Γ_F has compact image inside O^×_{Q̄_p}, so χ has no Galois-group parameter. The paper uses only the direction from Galois parameters, so the fix is right: state the correspondence with the Weil group, and restrict separately.

Confirmed (high). Item /76 states 'a complete intersection regular in codimension 3 is factorial'. The paper applies Grothendieck's theorem only to complete local rings (Corollary 15.22, p. 82: 'Since they are complete intersection … a theorem of Grothendieck implies the assertion; see [14]'). For non-local rings the statement is false. Z[√−5] = Z[t]/(t² + 5) is a regular Dedekind domain and a complete intersection, but it is not a UFD (6 = 2·3 = (1 + √−5)(1 − √−5), with all four factors irreducible and non-associate since the norm a² + 5b² never takes the values 2 or 3). The fix, the local complete-intersection version, is right.

Confirmed (high). On published pp. 53–54 the paper defines H_0 as the preimage of μ_{p−1} ⊂ T_2 under p_2 and asserts in Lemma 11.3 that H_0 is generalised reductive. The section allows p = 2: it 'is essentially [6, Lemma 4.2], but made to work for all F and not just Q_2', with κ algebraically closed of characteristic p for Proposition 11.5. For G = SL_2 over F̄_2 with P the Borel subgroup, the codimension-two hypotheses hold and μ_{p−1} = μ_1 = 1, so the scheme-theoretic preimage is ker(SL_2 → PGL_2) = μ_2, which is non-reduced in characteristic 2. It is not smooth, hence not generalised reductive. This is distinct from E1. The fix is right: use the reduced subgroup and propagate it into Proposition 14.5.

Confirmed (medium). On p. 54 the paper asserts that 'every cocharacter μ̄ … can be lifted to a cocharacter μ̃' through a finite map of centres. On pp. 55–56 it uses 'the unique cocharacter satisfying α∘p_2∘λ = id'. For G = SL_2 with L the diagonal torus, α∘p_2 on L is t ↦ t², so a cocharacter of L composes to t ↦ t^{2n}, and the identity is not attained. A positive multiple lifts, and the limit argument needs only a positive exponent. The fix is right.

Confirmed (medium). The proof of Lemma 11.4 (p. 55) prints γ·ē_21 = ωψ^{-1}ē_21 − ωψb²ē_12. Direct multiplication with ρ̃ = [[1,b],[0,ψ^{-1}]] gives ρ̃ e_21 ρ̃^{-1} = [[b, −ψb²],[ψ^{-1}, −b]] = b(e_11 − e_22) − ψb² e_12 + ψ^{-1} e_21. Modulo scalars, e_11 − e_22 ≡ 2e_11, so the term 2ωb ē_11 is missing; it vanishes only in characteristic 2. The flag ⟨ē_12⟩ ⊂ ⟨ē_12, ē_11⟩ ⊂ ad ρ remains stable with the same graded characters, so the lemma stands. The fix is right.

Confirmed (medium). At Tau Ceti f790474, TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Dynamic/Parabolic.lean defines parabolic (line 293), limit (332), levi (344) and unipotent (376), and proves limit_mem_levi (573), exists_mem_unipotent_mem_levi (629) and unipotent_sup_levi (635). Its variables are [CommSemiring R] [Semiring H] [HopfAlgebra R H] (line 82), with no reductivity or connectedness hypothesis. Dynamic/Functor.lean defines parabolicFunctor, leviFunctor and unipotentFunctor (lines 93–107) and their inclusions. Item /10's note misses these carriers. The fix, partial reuse while the scheme-theoretic statements remain to be planned, is right.

Confirmed (medium). The published paper cites [16, Example 1.1.16] (p. 51), [16, 5.3.9] and [16, 1.2.7] (p. 52) and [16, Theorem 4.1.7] (p. 63) for group-scheme facts. Its bibliography (p. 94) has [16] = Conrad, 'Irreducible components of rigid spaces' and [19] = Conrad, 'Reductive group schemes', and these numbers fit the latter. The fix is right: record the misbinding and cite 'Reductive group schemes' by title and locator.

Confirmed (medium). Appendix A.1 (p. 90) reads 'Let X: CRing → Set be an accessible presheaf … We denote by X(A) the condensed set obtained by composition X ∘ A'. The constant functor with value a two-element set is accessible, and composing it with a condensed ring gives the value 2 on the empty profinite set, where a condensed set must give a singleton. So the general claim fails. The application to affine schemes is fine, because representable functors satisfy X(0) = ∗ and preserve finite products. The fix, restricting to the representable affine functors used, is right.

Confirmed (medium). The prerequisite Paškūnas–Quast, 'generalised tori' (Forum Math. Sigma 13 (2025) e45), on p. 30 asserts in the proof of Lemma 8.4 'p_E^n ≅ O_E is isomorphic to O_F[Δ] as Z_p[Δ]-module', and the proof of Lemma 8.7 uses the same isomorphism of Δ-modules. By Noether's theorem this fails for wildly ramified E/F. For E = Q_2(√2), the trace on Z_2[√2] has image 2Z_2 in the invariants Z_2, while the norm of Z_2[C_2] is onto its invariants, so the modules are not isomorphic. The fix is right: use a rational normal basis for the rank count, and a cofinal family of normal-basis lattices inside the domain of exp for Lemma 8.7.
